messages:
support-oncall: Heads up — multiple customers reporting per-model throughput graphs in Console have flatlined to zero starting ~11:03 UTC. Tickets #9871, #9874. Affects models across regions. No increase in errors from API logs. Anyone seen this?

ana: investigating. which dashboards exactly? per-model throughput panels or the global one?

support-oncall: per-model throughput panels (by model label) — global total still shows activity. Users can still call the API successfully, latency normal. Only metric series that group by model are empty.

jeff: quick hypothesis: label rename or relabeling change in metrics pipeline. If the model label changed, Grafana panels that group_by label will show nothing. Any recent deploys to inference-proxy / metrics-agent around 11:00?

maria: I deployed inference-proxy v2.1.4 at 10:58 UTC to roll out a model identifier change. We replaced label model -> model_id to disambiguate variants. I forgot to add compatibility relabeling for metrics.

tilly: confirmed. scraped /metrics from a running proxy instance:
```
# HELP inference_requests_total total inference requests
inference_requests_total{model_id="gpt-mini",status="200",region="us-west-2"} 2543
```
expected was:
```
inference_requests_total{model="gpt-mini",status="200",region="us-west-2"} 2543
```
so prometheus no longer has a "model" label — panels group_by=model -> empty series.

devops-bot: (auto) grafana-alert: panel "Per-model throughput" firing: no series returned.

sre-lead: this explains why global totals are fine (they don't rely on model label). Impact: Console per-model breakdowns + billing UI per-model charts. Support team flagged customer confusion about possible usage drops.

ana: mitigation options: 1) add relabel_config in Prometheus scrape to copy model_id -> model, 2) rollback inference-proxy to v2.1.3, 3) update dashboards to use model_id (longer runway). Which do we want?

jeff: fastest is prometheus relabel to restore model label immediately. Example relabel_config (add to scrape job for proxies):
```
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__metrics_path__, model_id]
    regex: 
    separator: ";"
    target_label: model
    replacement: "$1"
    action: replace
```
That snippet is rough — we should use action: replace and source_labels: [model_id] -> target_label: model. I'll open a quick PR.

maria: rolling back is also simple but touches running traffic. We prefer in-place relabel since it's config-only on prometheus side.

support-oncall: customers want ETA. Any chance for a quick fix?

tilly: I can patch prometheus scrape config and push a hot-reload to prometheus in staging, verify dashboards return series, then apply to prod. Will need ~25m including verification.

sre-lead: do it. Also file changelog on the inference-proxy release notes — breaking metric label change. Add a note in release process to coordinate metrics label renames with observability.

devops-bot: (auto) deploy-job #542 started: prometheus hot-reload (staging).

ana: verification from staging: per-model panels repopulated after relabel applied. Confirmed mapping model_id -> model works for current metrics.

support-oncall: told customers we'll have dashboards back in ~30m. Putting on-hold for now.

jeff: PR opened to update scrape config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2112 — includes relabel_config and tests. Also adding acceptance test that dashboards still render when label changes.

maria: will follow up with a patch to inference-proxy that emits both labels for a deprecation period (model and model_id) so we don't need this forever. Planning v2.1.5 with dual-label output.

tilly: prod rollout completed at 11:30 UTC. Grafana panels show series again. Please verify customers' dashboards.

support-oncall: confirmed with customer in ticket #9871 — dashboard graphs restored. Closing the immediate incident, leaving follow-ups:
- infra#2112 merge + prod apply (permanent relabel)
- inference-proxy change to emit both labels (maria)
- release note & runbook update for metrics-label changes (sre-lead)

sre-lead: good. lesson: metrics label changes are effectively API changes for downstream observability. Let's require an observability compat plan for any future renames.

devops-bot: (auto) incident closed: #INC-2026.
